lines.trans: See you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; the plural أغاني (aghaani) is the one you hear most.

examples.trans: This is an old song my grandmother loves.
We listen to songs in the car every morning.

meanings.note: Means 'except / unless' (إلا إذا 'unless') and 'minutes to the hour' (اطنعش إلا خمسة 'five to twelve').

examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve!

examples.text: ما حدا بيقيس الساحة إلا مهندس!
examples.trans: Nobody measures a courtyard except an engineer!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ب- before nouns ('in/with'); with pronoun suffixes in Levantine it takes the stem في-: فيي ('in me'), فيك ('in/to you m.'), فيكي ('in/to you f.'), فيه ('in him/it'), فيها ('in her/it'), فينا ('in us'), فيهم ('in them').

examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!
My suitcase has a red ribbon in it.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: An imperative-only word: تعال to a man, تعالي to a woman, تعالوا to a group. Other tenses use إجا.

examples.trans: Come and sit next to me.
Come to the kitchen, all of you!

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حقيقية, plural: حقيقيين).

examples.trans: Did you book the room under your real name?
Let me show you my real work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: Means peace, safety, and is widely used as a greeting or farewell.

examples.text: يا سلام عالشمس الدافية بعد المطر!
examples.trans: Oh how lovely, warm sun after the rain!
They live in safety and peace in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شراشف.

examples.trans: We spread a clean white cloth on the table.
I brought fresh sheets from the closet.

meanings.note: Very common adverb in Jordanian Arabic for 'a little bit' or 'slowly'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of شيء; combines in كل شي ('everything'), أي شي ('anything'), ولا شي ('nothing').

examples.trans: Everything is ready on the table.

examples.text: رن الجرس إذا احتجت أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Standard word for morning in both Classical and colloquial Arabic.

examples.trans: Good morning! How did you sleep today?
The weather is very pleasant this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصلح, بيصلح).

examples.trans: I fix pipes and chairs.
Yesterday you fixed the old heater.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطوي, بيطوي).

examples.trans: Fold this sheet and put it in your pocket.
She folded the clean towels in the closet.

meanings.note: Used to describe a tall person or a long object.

examples.text: في رجال طويل واقف عند البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a tall man standing by the gate.
Three years was a long time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عتبات.

examples.trans: We found the suitcase on the doorstep.
We swept the stone threshold in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعزف, بيعزف).

examples.trans: I am still waiting for you to play the scale!

examples.text: الكبير كان يعزف بيانو كل جمعة.
examples.trans: The older boy used to play piano every Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غامقة, plural: غامقين).

examples.trans: The suitcase's color is dark blue.
A dark grey wool coat.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
The shelves are clean with no dust on them.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Refers to a lid, cover, or sometimes a blanket.

examples.trans: Put the lid on the pot.
In winter I sleep under a heavy blanket.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for singing; a song is أغنية.

examples.trans: My grandmother sings while she cooks.
We all sang at his birthday.

meanings.note: The Levantine everyday verb for entering a room or building (فوت! 'come in!'), where formal Arabic says دخل.

examples.trans: Come in, the door is open.
We went into the restaurant at eight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Describes something that shines: polished wood, clean glass, new shoes.

examples.trans: The floor is shiny after we mopped it.
He bought shiny black boots.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلاقي, بيلاقي).

examples.trans: Tell me how to find the hardware shop.

examples.text: لقيت هاد الصندوق الخشب ورا الحيط!
examples.trans: I found this wooden box behind the wall!

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Commonly used in Jordanian Arabic instead of the MSA word 'mughlaq'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, is the door locked?
The main water valve is shut off now.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: From قوس, an arch or bow: arched windows are شبابيك مقوسة.

examples.trans: The mosque's door is arched and tall.
They have old arched windows.

meanings.note: An inside hallway or a narrow passage between buildings.

examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
The hallway is dark, turn on the light.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for clean or tidy.

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the room is ready.

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water onto your clean floor.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واطية, plural: واطيين).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low wooden beam.
They spoke in a low voice for the guests' sake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Very common interjection used to urge action or to say goodbye ('yalla bye').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!
